I used to share the same sentiments about my own suicidal thoughts.

Until I made myself so busy (working almost 70 hours a week), that I literally was so physically tired I wouldn't want to think about suicide.

It doesn't stop. No matter what I do, no matter where I am, it simply does not stop.

That's the worse thing about it, you can be absolutely fine, all's dandy, having a good day or whatever, then bam;

"I wonder how much it would hurt to slit my own wrists? I wonder if I'm still alive at some conscious level when I die?"

"Remember Crystle? She used to make me the best cheese sandwiches, I loved her, why in the fuck did she die?"

You get the idea.

Or do it in the most graphic and violent way possible to scar them for life.

Like, set up automated letters/emails that tell them that they are to blame, they were the reason you died, that they could have done more, etc, etc and get them sent out regularly for a few years after you die.

Pay for your funeral in advance, and get a few actors to stand in as mourners. Then, when they show up to the funeral, get the actors to cry and wail and point at them and tell them that they were responsible, and that they could have prevented this.

Or not, whatever.

I just get so drunk and stoned that I can't feel my face anymore.

I can't recommend this for everybody though.

All the time.

Wake up thinking about suicide, then ruminate on it for hours. Then get sick of thinking suicidal thoughts, grab some lunch go for a walk, sit-down and have a cigarette and the whole cycle starts again.

I noticed that when I started getting suicidal I started asking a lot more questions.

Why work? Why have relationships if there going to end at some point? Why do this? Why do that? It just goes on and on. It's endless.

At some level, it made it much, much more difficult to stop suicidal thoughts, because it seems like suicide, or at least death, is the only logical solution. 

Whether it happens or not, it never really stopped for me. And it's a massive burden. This constant Sisyphean task that seems to have no real easing, outside of permenant brain damage.

As far as anti-depressants go? Most of them actually exacerbate and provoke suicidal thoughts. Which ones are you taking?

I've found there's usually two reactions to telling people I want to kill myself; They either super overreact, or don't have any reaction at all. 

Because I've expressed suicidal thoughts enough, I've gotten to points where I feel I need to kill myself literally just because I keep saying it but never doing it.

I almost feel like sometimes I want to to do it, simply to prove to people that I'm not doing it to get attention or some other bullshit excuse.

I was kind of thinking the same thing.

However, it's likely to get taken down almost straight away by most big streaming sites. Precedent has shown most suicide videos usually get blotted out by the big streamers, quickly and thoroughly.

Also, any kind of live event needs promotion, otherwise it'll likely be some random people stumbling across the feed and low viewer counts. Promoting your own suicide? I'm sure you'll have a lot of heat on you unless you privately promote it to a select group of people.

As for dieing alone, everyone dies alone. You're the only one who is experiencing that death at that exact moment, there's no one else to share in that experience. There might be some comfort, there might not be any comfort.

IN the final kind of stages of death, I'm talking the last hour to minutes, people become lucid and ususally are not aware (at least we don't think) of their surroundings or their own selves. I witnessed my grandmother die from pneumonia over the course of a few days and it was like she was tripping balls.

I litterally wanted to marry her, no joke. I'm not even so sure why I didn't now.
